lots.what_it_is: Raw sawn timber slab catalogued as 'SLAB OF HUON PINE', single board with mostly straight sawn edges and a little bark at the lower left, chalked 1126 2/10/26
lots.guide_summary: No evidence survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher logged no entries and my own WebSearch was refused (session budget 200 of 200 used). The Gowans bidsonline results page only lists special antique, art and currency sales, not general sales, so there is no Gowans slab result to compare. No currency rate used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Premium would be 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah, inbound freight $0, but a slab of this length needs a ute or trailer.
lots.confidence_reason: Species is the cataloguer's description only and cannot be confirmed from one photo; size is unmeasured; no market evidence of any kind was verified.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (researcher supplied no entries). The researcher's australianwoodwork.com.au page (finished products only) was rightly not logged.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo (photos/441120_1.jpg). Lot 1126 is the widest board in the row, there is no reliable scale, but against the iron cladding it looks about 2 to 2.4 m long and 40 to 50 cm wide, thickness not visible. Colour is an even pale straw-cream with fine circular saw marks, a small check at the top left, a small knot or bark inclusion at the left edge about a third up, and a short check at the bottom. Edges are largely square sawn, unlike neighbours 1125 and 1127 which are live edge with grey bark. Pale cream is not inconsistent with fresh-sawn Huon pine (which yellows with age), but nothing in the photo proves the species; the grain figure is mild.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, unfinished, appears sound apart from minor end and edge checks; moisture content and thickness unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the length, width and thickness of lot 1126, and whether it is known to be Huon pine (vendor provenance)? At Friday viewing, check for the distinctive Huon pine oily smell on a fresh scratch, fine even end grain, and any end splits or borer.
lots.score_reason: If genuinely Huon pine of this size, raw slabs can be worth several hundred dollars, but that is my general understanding only, not verified evidence; identification is unconfirmed and no price was seen, so scored mid-range and discounted.

lots.question_for_gowans: Is lot 1148 complete (display/knob unit, spool holder, nozzle kit, tools) and was it ever assembled or used? At viewing, check the second foam layer for the display unit and that the bed sticker film is intact.
lots.score_reason: Current budget printer, new for $279, so an opened unused example is likely worth roughly $120-200 secondhand (my estimate, not verified); 11 bids suggest competition.
